author: rule-family designer (world: a string of 6-10 coloured beads; lineup answer, revision 3)
description: BEAD-STRING RULE-FAMILY class in the LINEUP format, REVISION 3 (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md "Revision 3 (2026-09-05): beat the free-label attack", recipe for the other five lineup classes; iteration record in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_beads.md sec.15-22; v1 kept as tresk.v1.json, v2 as tresk.v2.json). CLUE = 2 example bead strings (3 on 0.2 % of clues), one per line, letters from R/G/B, 6-10 beads each; then a BLANK LINE; then FIVE candidate strings, one per line, all of the SAME length. ANSWER = the one candidate that obeys the hidden rule, written back verbatim (whitespace- and case-insensitive) or as its 1-based index 1-5. Exactly one candidate obeys the rule (500/500), so the floor is 20 %. WHY v2 HAD TO CHANGE: in lad-tresk-v2-1 and lad-ospren-v2-1 four Opus centaurs scored 79/81/83/86 % on tresk v2 without spending a single demo, with one engine - round 1 skip-harvest for base rates, round 2 answer a RANDOM candidate (a quarter come back correct: ~30 free gold labels, "30x what a demo gives"), then per clue keep every cheap predicate true of both examples and of EXACTLY ONE candidate, weight by rarity and answer the candidate the rarest survivor points at, learning from the labels which predicate uniquely explains a known-correct answer. Matched trap profiles (rev.2 sec.5b) and rarity-aware decoys (rev.2 sec.5c) were both already in v2 and both lost, for one reason: EVERY RULE OF v2's U WAS ITSELF A CHEAP PREDICATE IN THE ATTACKER'S BANK. Measured here against a 660-predicate reconstruction of the players' own bead banks (tresk1b's build_tresk()+extra_tresk(), ospren1a's f_tresk(), plus the obvious extensions), every rule of v2's U has best Jaccard 1.00 - "exactly n reds" is n_R==n, "the longest block is n" is maxrun==n, "exactly n blocks" is nruns==n, "it reads the same backwards" is palin, "all the blocks are the same size" is ndistinctrun==1, "as many R as G" is eq_RG. THE FIX (lever 3): PUT U OUTSIDE THE BANK - make the rules RELATIONS BETWEEN TWO BEADS, TWO CLUMPS OR TWO PLACES, which a (feature==value) bank cannot express, and aim the decoys at the attacker's RARITY order rather than his count. UNIVERSE U: 14 templates, 35 rules, ELEVEN of them relational (best bank Jaccard in brackets, density = the share of random strings of a random length 6-10 that obey it): (0) the 2nd bead and the 2nd-from-last bead are the same colour [.33, d.333]; (1) the biggest clump is the colour it starts with / ends with [.33, .295]; (2) the colour it starts with / ends with is all in one clump [.21, .136]; (3) the colour it starts with / ends with is the colour there is least of [.15, .099]; (4) every X bead has a Y bead right after it, 6 ordered pairs [.32, .112]; (5) there are just as many X clumps as Y clumps, 3 pairs [.35, .317]; (6) all the X beads come before all the Y beads, 6 ordered pairs [.25, .120]; (7) every clump is a different size from the clump next to it [.33, .128]; (8) the first two beads and the last two beads are the same pair [.12, .111]; (9) no bead has the same colour on both sides of it [.12, .103]; (10) the colour there is most of is all in one clump [.27, .078]; plus THREE CHEAP templates kept ON PURPOSE as the learnable slope and the continuity with v1/v2 - (11) there are exactly n C beads, n=4,5 [1.00, .163/.072] drawn at DOUBLE weight, (12) the biggest clump is exactly n beads long, n=4,5 [1.00, .097/.027], (13) only two colours are used [1.00, .135]. The three cheap templates take 30 % of clues; mean density of the hidden rule 0.154; template mix over 500 clues 23-39 each (cheap 79/37/36). U is an ANTICHAIN: brute-forced over ALL 88 209 strings of length 6-10 and over the generator's 14 916-string pool, 0 nesting violations, every rule with >= 2811 instances. Casualties of that check, recorded so they are not re-proposed: "the biggest clump is right at the start" is inside (1); "no two clumps are the same size" is inside (7); "the clumps get bigger/smaller as you go" is inside (7) and (1); "the first bead and the last bead are the only ones of their colour" is inside (0),(2),(5),(7); "the clump at the start and the clump at the end are the same size" is too dense (.502, J.62); "the colour it starts with is the one there is MOST of" is too dense (.430); "every X bead has a Y bead somewhere next to it" contains (4). EXCLUDED - 16 trap families, never in U, fitted to each clue (mean 8.30 fire per clue, min 4 max 14): no clump longer than the clue's longest (fits 100 %) - at least n R/G/B beads (100 %) - exactly the clue's set of colours (71 %) - all three colours appear (69 %) - more X beads than Y (69 %) - no two C beads ever touch (59 %) - it starts with / ends with the clue's colour (34 %/32 %) - exactly n clumps (19 %) - the two end beads are the same colour (10 %) - as many X beads as Y beads (8 %) - it alternates - all the clumps are the same size - it reads the same backwards - every bead has a neighbour of its own colour - each colour is all in one clump. NINE of those are v1/v2's own rules, retired because a single bank predicate says exactly the same thing. Matched trap profiles hold in the STRONG form: over 500 clues all 4149 fitted traps are satisfied by ALL FIVE candidates or by NONE, so no trap, no count of traps and no combination of traps separates the lineup, and a player whose universe is U plus the 16 traps is worth exactly a player who knows U. HOW THE LINEUP IS BUILT: five strings of one length; every decoy breaks the rule, fires exactly the same fitted traps as the true candidate and uses the same number of colours; then RANKS aims the true candidate's rank at a uniformly random place in THREE orders the attacker can build - first the RARITY order (the surprise of the rarest bank predicate that selects that candidate ALONE, i.e. what both revision-2 players actually ran), then the COUNT order (how many example-consistent bank predicates each candidate satisfies), then the LOOK-ALIKE order (bead-by-bead agreement with the other four). The 660-predicate bank is rebuilt inside generate() for exactly this purpose. MEASURED, 400-500 fresh clues, the full simulated attack (skip-harvest 300 clues -> random-candidate gold labels -> per-predicate unique-explanation weights -> rarity-weighted pick): 33.8 % at 0 labels, 41.2 % at 30, 41.8 % at 60, 42.0 % at 120, 45.8 % at 240 - flat, against v2's 83.8 / 89.8 / 90.5 / 91.5 / 91.0 % under the identical engine. The honest ceiling (the same engine with a bank that also contains all of U): 70.2 / 82.8 / 86.2 / 88.5 / 96.2 %, and U is learned to 90 % coverage in ~360 labels. The in-U intersection - a player who has mapped U - is 100.0 %. LEVERS (identical conditions, 400 clues, 60 labels): v3 as shipped 41.8 %; minus lever 3 (v2's own universe, as shipped) 90.5 %; minus lever 5 (decoys not aimed) 53.2 %; minus lever 1 (k=4) 48.5 %; minus lever 2 (three-example clues) 46.5 %; k=6 45.2 % (buys nothing, costs a clue line). So the relational universe is worth ~49 points, the rarity aiming ~11, the fifth candidate ~7, the two-example clue ~5. WITNESSES, 500 clues: in-U intersection 100.0 %; the true rule (solve) 100 % verbatim and 100 % by index; the candidate satisfying the MOST example-consistent bank predicates 20.4 %; the FEWEST 15.0 %; the medoid 15.6 %; the odd one out 21.4 %; candidate 1 19.2 %; a random candidate 17.6 %; the alphabetically first 25.6 %; the one most like an example bead-by-bead 22.0 %; the one with the most reds 25.0 %; the one with the most clumps 16.8 %; the one with the BIGGEST clump 33.0 % (the honest cost of keeping template 12 cheap); every excluded rule 17.9-22.7 % (all of it random tie-breaking, since the profiles are matched); a player who knows U minus its two rarest templates 91.8 %. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns the candidate that obeys it (nothing to vary: the answer is a choice). SCORE is 1019 chars (needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it splits the clue on the blank line, resolves an index or a verbatim candidate, rebuilds all 35 rules of U from a 149-character table, filters them by the examples, insists on a single survivor and checks that the CHOSEN CANDIDATE obeys it - a string that is not in the lineup scores 0, which is what kills the construction attack. Checked candidate-by-candidate against solve on 600 clues x 5 candidates x (verbatim + index + lower-case-with-spaces) = 9000 checks, 0 disagreements; rejects "", "0", "6", "9", "x", "1"*100, "R"*4000, the clue itself, unicode digits, "-1" and "1.0" without raising. No hidden channel.

# solve() re-derives the hidden rule exactly the way score() does -- rebuild U, keep the
# rules consistent with every example, insist on the single survivor -- and returns the one
# candidate that obeys it.  There is nothing left to vary: the answer is a choice.
PAIR = ("RG", "RB", "GR", "GB", "BR", "BG")
U = [(0, "--"), (7, "--"), (8, "--"), (9, "--"), (10, "--"), (13, "--")] \
    + [(t, x) for t in (1, 2, 3) for x in ("0-", "1-")] \
    + [(t, x) for t in (4, 6) for x in PAIR] \
    + [(5, x) for x in ("RG", "RB", "GB")] \
    + [(11, x + n) for x in "RGB" for n in "45"] + [(12, "-" + n) for n in "45"]


def p(r, w):
    t, q = r
    G = [(k, len(list(g))) for k, g in itertools.groupby(w)]
    R = [l for _, l in G]
    N = lambda x: sum(1 for k, _ in G if k == x)
    M = max(R)
    C = sorted((w.count(x), x) for x in "RGB")
    e = w[0] if q[0] == "0" else w[-1]
    return [w[1] == w[-2],                                    # 0  2nd == 2nd-from-last
            {k for k, l in G if l == M} == {e},               # 1  the biggest clump's colour
            N(e) == 1,                                        # 2  that colour is one clump
            C[0][0] < C[1][0] and C[0][1] == e,               # 3  that colour is the rarest
            q[0] in w and all(w[i:i + 2] == q for i in range(len(w)) if w[i] == q[0]),  # 4
            q[0] in w and q[1] in w and N(q[0]) == N(q[1]),   # 5  as many X clumps as Y clumps
            q[0] in w and q[1] in w and w.rfind(q[0]) < w.find(q[1]),   # 6  all X before all Y
            all(x != y for x, y in zip(R, R[1:])),            # 7  neighbouring clumps differ
            w[:2] == w[-2:],                                  # 8  the two end pairs match
            not any(w[i] == w[i + 2] for i in range(len(w) - 2)),       # 9  no sandwiched bead
            C[2][0] > C[1][0] and N(C[2][1]) == 1,            # 10 the commonest, one clump
            str(w.count(q[0])) == q[1],                       # 11 exactly n C beads   (cheap)
            str(M) == q[1],                                   # 12 the biggest clump    (cheap)
            len(set(w)) == 2][t]                              # 13 only two colours     (cheap)


def solve(clue):
    B = clue.strip().split("\n\n")
    E = B[0].split()
    K = B[1].split()
    V = [r for r in U if all(p(r, e) for e in E)]
    for k in K:
        if p(V[0], k):
            return k
    return K[0]
